features.name: is_top_resource
features.description: Indicator for the most frequently requested resources in the training set.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a direct linear margin for highly common resources which may have distinct baseline approval patterns.

features.name: is_top_mgr
features.description: Indicator for the managers with the highest volume of access requests.
features.expected_model_benefit: Allows the linear SVM to adjust the decision boundary for high-volume managers.

features.name: is_default_role_rollup_1
features.description: Flags if the request belongs to the overwhelmingly dominant ROLE_ROLLUP_1 category.
features.expected_model_benefit: Creates a strong binary feature for the most common organizational rollup, useful for establishing a baseline margin.

features.name: role_title_code_diff
features.description: Absolute difference between ROLE_TITLE and ROLE_CODE, capturing potential hierarchical or sequential relationships in the anonymized IDs.
features.expected_model_benefit: Allows the linear SVM to capture proximity or exact matches between role title and code as a continuous severity measure.

features.name: is_top_role_deptname
features.description: Indicator for the most common department names.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a linear shift for requests originating from the largest departments.

features.name: is_top_role_family
features.description: Flags if the role family is the most frequent one in the dataset.
features.expected_model_benefit: Helps the model isolate the largest role family for a specific weight adjustment.

features.name: resource_mgr_cooccurrence_score
features.description: Semantic judgment of the typicality of the requested RESOURCE for the given MGR_ID, based on historical co-occurrence frequencies.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a continuous typicality measure that helps the SVM establish a margin based on request normality.

features.name: role_combination_rarity
features.description: An anomaly score evaluating how unusual the combination of ROLE_DEPTNAME, ROLE_TITLE, and ROLE_FAMILY is, with higher values indicating rarer combinations.
features.expected_model_benefit: Acts as a continuous severity measure for unusual role configurations, which is highly effective for linear models.

features.name: manager_team_size_estimate
features.description: Estimated general access broadness for the specific MGR_ID, representing how many unique resources the manager's reports typically request.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a normalized score representing manager scope, allowing the SVM to scale its confidence based on manager experience.

features.name: resource_request_frequency_normalized
features.description: A continuous score representing the global popularity of the RESOURCE, normalized between 0 and 1.
features.expected_model_benefit: Transforms a high-cardinality categorical into a smooth continuous feature ideal for linear projections.

features.name: role_rollup_hierarchy_diff
features.description: Absolute difference between ROLE_ROLLUP_1 and ROLE_ROLLUP_2 IDs, capturing structural distance in the organizational hierarchy.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a continuous distance metric between two levels of the role hierarchy for the SVM to weight.

features.name: is_common_role_family_desc
features.description: Indicator for the most common role family description.
features.expected_model_benefit: Isolates the dominant role family description to provide a stable linear offset.
